title: Co-error Mode Surgery for Stable VLA–World-Model Co-Adaptation
hook: A VLA–WAM loop can improve imagined return while a small set of reciprocal co-error modes predicts worse physical task success. Removing only those positive-loop-gain modes from the joint update should reverse the physical-success trend without discarding the remaining imagined-learning signal.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal: the named contrast is rising imagined return versus falling LIBERO/RoboCasa physical success, stratified by the signed reciprocal loop gain defined below. Shape (c) was viable because the intervention removes only a low-rank update subspace, but it was rejected because no pre-existing baseline axis establishes that this is strictly smaller before measurement.

gap_closure.gap: Even after the WorldSync action-faithfulness and Feedback World Model correction moves, no retrieved leaf establishes whether the residual world-model error is aligned with the policy's improvement direction across successive updates; small average prediction error can still be concentrated exactly where the policy finds high imagined advantage -- stakes: apparently faithful rollouts can drive unsafe or ineffective actions at deployment, and the field cannot infer policy-learning validity from world-model accuracy alone.
gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin in VLA–WAM co-training and C04's closest exemplars concern compression; we instantiate its error/sensitivity split by decomposing a tentative reciprocal update into positive-loop-gain co-error modes versus task-supported bulk, then the structural companion ships a constrained optimizer that cancels only the amplifying minority.

core_mechanism: At co-training cycle t, let πθ be the open-weight VLA policy and Mψ the action-conditioned video WAM, and obtain the ordinary tentative updates uπ and uM from the existing VLAW-style real/imagined objectives without applying them. On current-policy LIBERO or RoboCasa simulator snapshots, encode both Mψ's predicted next observation and the simulator next observation with Mψ's frozen observation encoder and form residual vectors e; randomized SVD gives orthonormal residual modes qj, with rank k chosen as the smallest rank up to k_max = 8 that explains an energy fraction ρ = 0.90, where ρ is swept over {0.80, 0.90, 0.95}. For each qj, inject paired latent interventions ±ηqj into Mψ's predicted next-state feature during the imagined objective, with η = 0.01 times that layer's residual RMS and selected by the sweep {0.005, 0.01, 0.02}, and recompute one policy-gradient vector; their centered difference defines the WAM-to-policy susceptibility and its induced action direction vij. From the same current snapshots, execute paired simulator actions ai ± εvij/||vij||, with ε = 0.05 of each action dimension's valid range and selected by the sweep {0.02, 0.05, 0.10}, then project the centered change in physical next-state residual onto qj to obtain the policy-to-environment residual response. Their unit-canceling product gj is the signed reciprocal co-error loop gain: gj > 0 means a WAM residual perturbation moves the policy toward actions whose physical residual grows in the same mode, while gj < 0 is locally self-correcting. Using a probe budget b = 64 paired snapshots per cycle, increased to b = 128 only when the two half-batch estimates disagree in sign, partition modes into sign-stable positive-gain modes A and the remaining bulk S. Replace the independent application of uπ and uM with a whitened joint quadratic projection that minimally changes both tentative updates subject to the first-order constraints gj + cj,π·(ũπ-uπ) + cj,M·(ũM-uM) ≤ 0 for every j in A, where the sensitivity rows cj are obtained by automatic differentiation through the paired intervention calculation; whitening by each update block's RMS makes the distance dimensionless. Apply ũπ and ũM together, so the intervention changes the next deployed policy action and the next WAM rather than merely changing a diagnostic score. Under a locally accurate response linearization and sign-stable paired probes, the constraint removes positive first-order residual feedback, while the projection-distance inequality bounds first-order degradation of the original task objective by ||∇Ltask||·||ũ-u||; no global stability or unbiasedness claim is made outside current-policy simulator support.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger:
P1. A small residual-mode minority carries most harmful reciprocal coupling; this is plausible because contact failures are sparse and mode-concentrated, but it is untested — falsification target.
P2. Paired ± latent injections remain inside Mψ's locally meaningful representation neighborhood; the η sweep tests this rather than assuming it.
P3. The simulator's paired next-state response is an adequate physical intervention oracle for LIBERO/RoboCasa; transfer to real robots is empirical, not guaranteed.
OBSERVATION-MODEL. Snapshot states are sampled from the current policy's visitation distribution and paired actions are generated from the local response direction, so the sample is deliberately local and is not unbiased for future policies or unvisited deployment states; claims are restricted to one-cycle behavior on current-policy support.
ESTIMAND. For each residual mode qj, gj is the one-cycle, current-policy-distribution directional derivative from a WAM latent residual perturbation through the induced VLA action change to the same mode's simulator-observed next-state residual, averaged over current-policy reset snapshots.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT:
The naive runnable version gates or downweights imagined rollouts with large WAM prediction error or uncertainty before taking the usual alternating updates. Branch (i): it silently assumes scalar error magnitude identifies directional coupling, which is false when small residuals align with the policy-improvement direction while large orthogonal residuals do not; Co-error Mode Surgery confronts this by measuring the signed bidirectional response and modifying the coupled update itself. The quadratic projection is a standard constrained-optimization tool, but the unsolved domain structure is that each constraint coefficient composes a differentiable WAM→policy response with a budgeted physical policy→environment response under changing robot visitation, so neither generic gradient surgery nor generic small-gain control supplies the estimator. The design explicitly avoids Dyna mixing, DAgger aggregation, short-horizon or conservative MBRL, uncertainty filtering, target-network lag, generic cross-fitting, and naive alternating training named as occupied lineage nodes.
BLOCK 3 — DESIGN RATIONALE:
The anchor is treated as one mechanism because the same qj basis supports diagnosis, intervention, and the fidelity bound; adding adaptive-censoring or global sign-identification modules would introduce separate estimands and weaken falsifiability. I rejected a frozen anchor-set/phase-scaffold evaluator because it would be a holdout-style benchmark rather than an intervention, and rejected policy-only clipping because it cannot break a reciprocal mode carried jointly by uπ and uM.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Load an existing open-weight VLA/WAM pair configured for LIBERO or RoboCasa, collect the current cycle's real/simulator transition batch, and compute but do not apply the ordinary VLA update uπ and WAM update uM; output the tentative joint update u.
2. On b current-policy simulator snapshots, run Mψ and the simulator for the same actions, encode both next observations with Mψ's frozen observation encoder, and output the residual matrix E.
3. Run randomized SVD on E, select k using k_max and ρ, and output residual modes {qj} plus their explained-energy distribution; this tests whether a high-impact minority exists.
4. For every qj, inject ±ηqj at the named WAM next-feature interface, rerun the imagined loss backward pass, and output the centered policy-gradient response and induced current-policy action directions vij.
5. Clone each current simulator snapshot, execute the paired actions defined by ±εvij, encode the two resulting next observations, and output the centered physical residual response along qj.
6. Multiply the two directional responses in matched units to output gj, split the probe batch in half for sign stability, and partition modes into A and S; if signs disagree, repeat only this probe with b = 128.
7. Differentiate each sign-stable positive gj with respect to the tentative joint update, assemble the sensitivity rows cj, and solve the whitened quadratic projection for ũ under the nonpositive first-order loop-gain constraints.
8. Apply ũπ to the VLA and ũM to the WAM in the same optimizer commit, then deploy the changed VLA for the next rollout cycle and log both physical task success and imagined return.
9. For the negative-control arm, permute qj-to-physical-response pairings before Step 7 while preserving mode values and update norm; apply its projected update to a separate seed so any downstream benefit cannot be attributed to generic shrinkage.
10. Compare against the unchanged VLAW-style alternating commit, policy-only norm matching, and scalar-error gating, reporting mode-gain distribution, projection distance, imagined return, and simulator task success.
falsification_prediction: Run three co-training cycles for the same open-weight VLA/WAM initialization on existing LIBERO and RoboCasa tasks, comparing the ordinary VLAW-style alternating update, scalar-error gating, norm-matched policy-only shrinkage, and Co-error Mode Surgery; after every cycle measure simulator task success rate and imagined return. If the mechanism is correct, physical task success increases relative to the three baselines while the upper tail of signed reciprocal loop gain gj decreases, even in runs where imagined return rises in every arm. The one load-bearing variable is the matched per-mode reciprocal loop gain gj. As a negative-control intervention, permute the pairing between each WAM→policy response and its physical policy→environment response before constructing the projection; this preserves marginal response magnitudes and update norm but should return downstream task success toward the ordinary alternating baseline, which would falsify the claim if the permuted control retains the gain.
compute_budget: 28 GPU-day on 80GB-class GPUs for two benchmarks, four arms, three co-training cycles, probe sweeps, and repeated seeds; $0 paid-API cost because evaluation uses simulator success and open-weight model signals.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: VLAW alternates real-rollout WAM refinement with synthetic VLA improvement, whereas this candidate estimates a signed WAM→policy→physical-residual loop gain and projects the joint update against its positive modes.

World-Gymnast optimizes VLM-scored WAM rollouts, whereas this candidate intervenes on latent residual modes and uses paired simulator responses to prevent jointly compatible dynamics/reward errors from steering the update.

RISE separates controllable dynamics from progress value to produce imagined advantages, whereas this candidate composes their downstream policy susceptibility with physical residual response and cancels only sign-positive reciprocal modes.

WorldSync aligns generated intervention effects with ground-truth action consequences, whereas this candidate measures how a residual intervention changes the next policy update and constrains both learners when that closed response amplifies the same error mode.

Feedback World Model corrects inference-time latent predictions from observed next states without parameter updates, whereas this candidate changes the coupled VLA and WAM parameter update using a signed reciprocal-response constraint.

what_step_was_missed: WorldSync would need to compose its action-intervention residual with the VLA update induced by that residual, estimate the resulting dimensionless signed loop gain under paired physical probes, and constrain the joint VLA/WAM update against positive modes.
